newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees '97 basic grains output at 33 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees '97 basic grains output at 33 mln T.

text.p: Output of 10 basic grains and oilseeds in Mexico is expected to rise six percent in the 1997 farm cycle to 33 million tonnes, Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida Ochoa said.
In a statement obtained Tuesday, Labastida said the crop forecast was based on the premise the country would receive similar rainfall levels to 1996 when the country produced 31.2 million tonnes.
The 1.8-million-tonne increase in basic grains and oilseeds would come through additional production of corn, beans, wheat, sorghum and soybeans.

Labastida said the bulk of the increased output would come from the country's autumn-winter planting cycle, rising to more than 10 million tonnes compared to the less than nine million tonnes in the 1996 cycle.
"That means the production from the autumn winter cycle will be 1.5 million tonnes above the same cycle from the previous year, an increase of 16 percent," he added.
Mexico has two planting cycles because the country has such a diverse climate. One is the autumn-winter cycle and the other is the spring-summer cycle.
Labastida said the Agriculture Ministry has estimated that by 2000, Mexican production of its 10 basic grains and oilseeds will be between 37 million and 38 million tonnes.
Currently, Mexico consumes around 35 million tonnes, and demand is growing.

"There will be a large increase in demand and we hope to win the (production vs demand) race. This represents a great opportunity for the farm sector because farmers will have the chance to produce, trade and sell what they grow, although we are aware it is a big challenge," Labastida said.
